# Define and publish the common inference audit event schema

## Description

This epic defines the common audit event schema for model inference traffic and publishes it so that both current and future emitting components (pipelines, workbenches) can produce compatible events. The schema specifies the structured fields every audit event must carry — caller identity, model and version, timestamp, and response status — and explicitly excludes payload content, consistent with the compliance requirement to record requests without capturing inference payloads.

## Scope

- Define a versioned audit event schema capturing: caller identity, model, model version, timestamp, and response status.
- Explicitly document that request/response payloads are out of the schema.
- Design the schema to be extensible so future components (Data Science Pipelines, workbenches) can emit compatible events without breaking existing consumers.
- Publish the schema in the appropriate component repository so consuming implementations and documentation can reference it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The schema is defined, reviewed, and published in a component repository artifact that downstream implementations can build against.
- Every field required by the inference audit requirement (caller identity, model/version, timestamp, response status) is present in the schema.
- The schema carries no inference payload fields.
- The schema is extensible for adoption by non-inference components in future strategies.
- The schema is versioned.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4** (P2): A common audit event schema is defined and published so future components emit compatible events.
- Note: this epic is the prerequisite for the inference emission requirement (HLR-1), which requires its events to conform to this schema; it is therefore prioritized as the highest priority of the HLRs it transitively enables.

# KServe inference audit event emission and reliable delivery

## Description

This epic implements audit event emission in the KServe model serving stack so that every inference request through a KServe endpoint produces a structured audit event, and delivers those events to the cluster audit sink reliably. This is the core compliance capability: auditors get a structured record of who invoked which model endpoint, when, and with what outcome, delivered with at-least-once semantics to the cluster audit sink (tamper-evidence of the stored record is out of scope for this epic; see the decomposition summary's health warnings for human verification of that requirement).

## Scope

- Emit an audit event for every inference request routed through a KServe InferenceService endpoint, in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- Each event captures caller identity, model and version, timestamp, and response status — no request or response payloads.
- Events conform to the published common audit event schema.
- Deliver events to the cluster audit sink (the standard cluster logging forwarder) with at-least-once semantics.
- Buffer events so they are not lost on component restart.
- Define the per-project audit enablement/disable configuration surface that the serving path honors, for use by administrators (surfaced in the Dashboard by separate work).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every inference request through a KServe endpoint (serverless and raw deployment modes) results in an audit event containing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status.
- No audit event contains request or response payload content.
- All events conform to the published common audit event schema.
- Events are delivered to the standard cluster logging forwarder with at-least-once semantics: an event may be duplicated but is never dropped.
- Events emitted shortly before a component restart are not lost — buffered events survive restart and are delivered.
- The per-project audit enablement/disable configuration is honored by the serving path: when auditing is disabled for a project, no audit events are emitted for that project's inference traffic.
- Build pipeline is green for the modified repositories.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1** (P0): Every inference request through a KServe endpoint emits an audit event capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status (not payloads).
- **HLR-2** (P0): Audit events are delivered to the cluster audit sink with at-least-once semantics and are not lost on component restart.

# Dashboard per-project inference auditing controls

## Description

This epic adds administrator-facing controls in the Dashboard to enable and disable inference auditing per project. Administrators manage the audit configuration through the existing Dashboard project administration surfaces; the serving side honors the configured state.

## Scope

- Add a per-project control (within existing Dashboard project settings/administration surfaces) for administrators to enable and disable inference auditing for that project.
- Persist the control state via the Dashboard's existing configuration mechanism (Kubernetes CRs / feature-flag configuration).
- Surface the current auditing state for a project in the Dashboard.
- Restrict the control to administrator access, consistent with existing Dashboard RBAC patterns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable and disable inference auditing for a project from the Dashboard.
- The control's state is persisted and reflected accurately when the Dashboard is reloaded or revisited.
- The control is restricted to administrators; non-administrative project users cannot change the auditing state.
- When auditing is enabled for a project via the Dashboard, inference requests on that project's KServe endpoints produce audit events; when disabled, they do not.
- Build pipeline is green for the modified repository.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3** (P1): Administrators can enable/disable inference auditing per project from the Dashboard.

# Document enabling and interpreting inference auditing

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for inference auditing: how administrators enable and disable auditing per project from the Dashboard, how inference audit events flow to the cluster audit sink, and how to interpret the event fields. This is substantive new content authoring (new documentation topics), distinct from the code implementation work.

## Scope

- New documentation topic(s) covering:
  - What inference auditing records (caller identity, model/version, timestamp, response status) and what it deliberately does not record (payloads).
  - How to enable and disable inference auditing per project from the Dashboard, including required administrator role.
  - How events are delivered to the cluster audit sink (standard cluster logging forwarder) and the at-least-once delivery semantics.
  - Reference documentation for the common audit event schema fields and how to interpret each field.
  - Guidance for compliance reviewers on verifying the audit trail.
- Follow the Red Hat docs content process and tooling for authoring and publishing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers enabling and disabling inference auditing per project from the Dashboard.
- Documentation covers interpreting audit events, including a field-by-field reference of the common audit event schema.
- Documentation notes that payloads are not captured and that delivery is at-least-once (duplicates are possible).
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of the inference audit emission and the Dashboard controls.
- Documentation builds and publishes cleanly through the docs content pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5** (P2): Documentation covers enabling auditing and interpreting events.
